blurb: Gold-weight traders of the forest belt, famous for kente cloth and the Golden Stool.

clues.greeting: Akwaaba! — the word that welcomes you at every door.
clues.dress: Hand-woven strip cloth in gold, green and black, each pattern with its own name.
clues.food: Pounded cassava and plantain served with light, peppery soup.
clues.music: Talking drums that can recite proverbs and the names of kings.
clues.symbols: Adinkra stamps: Gye Nyame, Sankofa and dozens more.

blurb: A nation forged in the nineteenth century, known for its beadwork and harmonies.

clues.dress: Colourful beadwork whose colours spell out messages.
clues.food: Stiff maize porridge with amasi, fermented milk.
clues.symbols: The cowhide shield and short stabbing spear.

blurb: City builders of the forest and savanna, with a vast pantheon and a talking-drum tradition.

clues.greeting: Ẹ káàárọ̀ — good morning, with a bow or kneel to elders.
clues.dress: Agbada robes and tall gele head-ties for celebrations.
clues.food: Pounded yam with egusi melon-seed stew.
clues.music: Jùjú and fújì, led by the dùndún talking drum.
clues.symbols: Bronze heads of an ancient sacred city.
